profile.name: Speech to text (transcriptions and captions)
profile.description: Transcribes audio and video into timed SRT captions. Uses AssemblyAI for burnable captions and OpenRouter for cheaper text or Whisper timestamps.

memory.content: This bot transcribes audio and video into timed SRT caption files, using cheap OpenRouter models and AssemblyAI as the quality baseline.

OpenRouter nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 cannot return timestamps (verbose_json 400); it is text-only. For timed SRT on OpenRouter use openai/whisper-1 word-level timestamps. AssemblyAI universal-3-5-pro remains the better caption baseline.

STT bake-off on a 3-minute VO: AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro ~$0.21/hr is best for burnable SRT (native short cues); Parakeet nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 ~$0.09/hr is cheapest text but no timestamps; Whisper Large V3 ~$0.027/hr has timestamps but unusable paragraph-length cues; openai/whisper-1 ~$0.36/hr makes real short cues but costs more than AssemblyAI. Use AssemblyAI for captions to burn; Parakeet only for cheap untimed text.
Uses OpenRouter speech-to-text at https://openrouter.ai via a connector secret (openrouter / api_key). Request the key on first run.
Uses AssemblyAI at https://www.assemblyai.com via a connector secret (assemblyai / api_key). Request the key on first run. Default speech model is universal-3-5-pro.

skills.name: OpenRouter STT
skills.description: Use this when transcribing audio or video into a timed SRT caption file via OpenRouter speech-to-text.
skills.content:
---
name: OpenRouter STT
description: >-
  Use this when transcribing audio or video into a timed SRT caption file via
  OpenRouter speech-to-text.
---
Turn audio or video into a timed .srt file via OpenRouter transcription.

## Auth

Read the OpenRouter API key from this agent’s connector secret (`openrouter` / `api_key`). Never print or paste the key.

`Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY`

If the key is missing, request it with a secret-request (`connector`: `openrouter`, `field`: `api_key`) and stop until it is provided.

## What actually works (verified 2026-09-01)

- **`nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3` is text-only on OpenRouter.** `response_format=verbose_json` returns 400: model does not support verbose_json. Cheap (~$0.09/hr) but **cannot make SRT**.
- **`openai/whisper-large-v3`** returns `verbose_json` segments and is very cheap, but segments are long paragraphs with dropped phrases. Not caption-usable without word-level reflow.
- **Timed SRT default:** `openai/whisper-1` with `timestamp_granularities: ["word","segment"]`, then pack words into ~42-char / ~5s cues. ~$0.36/hr, more than AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro ($0.21/hr).
- **Quality baseline for captions:** AssemblyAI `universal-3-5-pro` (see AssemblyAI STT skill). Native SRT export, short cues. Prefer this when the user wants captions they can burn.

Do **not** use `openai/gpt-transcribe`, `openai/gpt-4o-transcribe`, or `openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` for captions. They return text only, no timestamps.

## Endpoint

`POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/audio/transcriptions`

`response_format` must be `verbose_json`. Native `srt`/`vtt` is rejected (400). Build SRT yourself from `words` (preferred) or `segments`.

`verbose_json` timestamps only work on OpenAI, Groq, and Together. Other providers 400. Do not rely on `provider.order` / `only` — the STT endpoint ignores them.

## Prepare the file

1. Copy the user’s audio/video onto the box if needed.
2. If it is video, extract audio with ffmpeg: `ffmpeg -y -i input -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 64k /workspace/stt-audio.mp3`
3. Platform caps: multipart **25 MB**; ~**60s upstream processing timeout** — split long files into ~5–10 min compressed chunks. Offset timestamps when stitching.
4. No audio URLs. Send base64 JSON or multipart file only.

## Request (word-level SRT)

```json
{
  "model": "openai/whisper-1",
  "input_audio": { "data": "<raw base64, not a data URI>", "format": "mp3" },
  "language": "en",
  "response_format": "verbose_json",
  "timestamp_granularities": ["word", "segment"]
}
```

Multipart (`-F file=@clip.mp3`) is fine under 25 MB. Pass `language` only if the user named one.

## SRT from `words`

Pack `words` into cues of ~32–42 characters or ~4–7 seconds, or a pause >0.6s. Cue start = first word `start`, end = last word `end`.

```python
def srt_ts(sec: float) -> str:
    ms = int(round(float(sec) * 1000))
    h, ms = divmod(ms, 3_600_000)
    m, ms = divmod(ms, 60_000)
    s, ms = divmod(ms, 1000)
    return f"{h:02d}:{m:02d}:{s:02d},{ms:03d}"
```

If only `segments` exist, emit those but warn the user if cues are longer than ~7s.

Write `/workspace/<stem>.srt` and attach that file in chat. Mention model, duration, and `usage.cost` if present.

## Compare with AssemblyAI

When asked to compare, run AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro on the same file (see AssemblyAI STT skill) and report cue count, cost, and wording diffs. Do not claim Parakeet produced the SRT.

## Errors

401 invalid key, 402 no credits, 400 `verbose_json` unsupported on that model/provider, 404 unknown model, 413 file too large, 429 rate limit, 502 upstream. Retry 429/502 with backoff. Never leak the key in error text.

skills.name: AssemblyAI STT
skills.description: Use this when transcribing audio or video to a timed SRT via AssemblyAI, or when comparing AssemblyAI quality against OpenRouter.
skills.content:
---
name: AssemblyAI STT
description: >-
  Use this when transcribing audio or video to a timed SRT via AssemblyAI, or
  when comparing AssemblyAI quality against OpenRouter.
---
Turn audio or video into a timed .srt file via AssemblyAI. Use this as the quality baseline, and when comparing against OpenRouter.

## Auth

Read the API key from this agent’s connector secret (`assemblyai` / `api_key`). Never print or paste the key.

Header: `Authorization: $ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY` (raw key, not Bearer).

If the key is missing, request it with a secret-request (`connector`: `assemblyai`, `field`: `api_key`) and stop until it is provided.

## Default model

- **Default:** `universal-3-5-pro` (flagship, ~$0.21/hour). Word timestamps included. Native SRT export.
- **Cheaper:** `universal-2` (~$0.15/hour) only if the user asks to save cost.

Speech understanding extras (diarization, keyterms, medical) cost extra. Do not enable them unless asked.

## Flow

1. Upload local audio: `POST https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/upload` with the raw file bytes and `Authorization` header. Response `upload_url`.
2. Create transcript: `POST https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript` JSON `{"audio_url": "<upload_url>", "speech_models": ["universal-3-5-pro"]}`. Response `id`.
3. Poll `GET https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript/<id>` until `status` is `completed` or `error`. Sleep 2–3s between polls.
4. Export SRT: `GET https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript/<id>/srt?chars_per_caption=42`
5. Plain text is `text` on the completed transcript. Word timings are in `words[]` (`text`, `start`, `end` in milliseconds).

Write `/workspace/<stem>.srt` and `/workspace/<stem>.txt`. Attach the SRT in chat. Mention duration and that the model was AssemblyAI.

## Compare with OpenRouter

When the user wants a comparison, run AssemblyAI on the same file as OpenRouter (Parakeet for cheap text, whisper-1 for timed SRT). Report side by side: model, $/hour estimate, cue count, and obvious quality diffs. Do not claim WER unless both transcripts are scored.

## Errors

401 bad key, 400 bad request, 429 rate limit. Never leak the key in error text.
